So that's sort of our implementation plan of the new act until 2021. Oh, sorry, I could, I was hearing my own voice. The other thing that's been, I've been working on quite a bit is the Pierce County Forest Investigation Team. And that is the new county-wide team and that's established to meet the state criteria, the new state law for investigating officer deadly uses of force. Involves every law enforcement agency in the county to include the state patrol. It's no small feat to get all those agencies on the same page. So far, we're moving along pretty well. We've actually had one official activation for Tacoma's last officer-involved shooting. Knock on wood, things went fairly smoothly. We're still in the process of developing protocols and getting everything in place to actually meet the WAC and the whole law, but we're definitely making progress. Another thing that's sort of front and center for me right now is the city's budget. We've got, it's been proposed for the 21-22. Our proposed budget's out there. We have presentations next Wednesday, I believe, to the council or I do on just the police department budget. So hopefully we can get through that. We're still trying to overcome a lot of the economic impacts of COVID. So we're not sure what the next two years is gonna hold completely with that in mind. One of the things that was impacted this year was hiring. We had two entry-level officers that we actually had conditional offers out to, and we had to retract those or at least freeze them until we got through a lot of the COVID stuff, until we had a good handle on the impacts of COVID or the economic impacts. We'll see what happens when we get through the next couple of weeks, if we're able to unfreeze those and bring them on and get them to the academy, but that's been a pretty big impact for us. Still dealing with the, speaking of COVID, some of the new protocols related to COVID and reminding everybody not to get complacent and use precautions when you're out in the public and around each other and keep in mind what constitutes an exposure. A lot of that, we did have our assistant chief go, John Unford go to Wenatchee with the Pierce County Incident Management Team to help them manage their COVID outbreak that they were having.
